biography.plain_text: Donald C. McGraw Jr. was an American publisher and grandson of McGraw-Hill cofounder James H. McGraw. He rose through the family company to lead international publishing before establishing Nautical Quarterly with collaborators. His later work connected publishing with maritime history, while his longstanding support of Mystic Seaport extended that interest into museum life.

long_biography.plain_text:
In 1984, publisher Donald C. McGraw Jr. bought into Soundings when recession and an overambitious expansion had left the boating newspaper in financial difficulty. During his ownership, it added waterfront coverage and Woodshop News, recovered profitability and eventually passed to Trader Publishing. McGraw was the majority owner at the time of the sale.

A Navy veteran of the Pacific war, he credited that service with teaching him leadership. Maritime preservation became another enduring commitment. As the first chairman of Mystic Seaport's National Council of Advisors, he supported its endowment and helped enrich its collection of J.E. Buttersworth paintings. His own collecting reflected the same interest in preserving the art and artifacts of seafaring.
